BRS Leader KTR Blames Government Inefficiency for Telangana Drought Conditions

29 Oct 2026, 10:43 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Public Services Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Allegations of Administrative Failure

Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao has publicly attributed the prevailing drought-like conditions across Telangana to administrative shortcomings rather than natural causes. Speaking at Telangana Bhavan during an event where several political figures from the Nirmal constituency joined the BRS, Rao asserted that agricultural distress across the state stems directly from inadequate resource management.

According to the opposition leader, agricultural producers are encountering substantial difficulties due to deficits in irrigation water supply, electricity availability, and essential fertilizers such as urea. He stated that the current administration has neglected to resolve these fundamental operational challenges.

Water Management and Irrigation Concerns

Central to Rao's critique was the management of major river systems. He alleged that despite adequate flow levels in both the Godavari and Krishna rivers, significant volumes of water have remained unutilized and flowed into the sea instead of being channeled toward agricultural lands.

Furthermore, the BRS leader claimed that authorities have declined to operate the pumps associated with the Kaleshwaram lift irrigation project, contributing directly to crop damage. He noted that agricultural producers in certain areas have resorted to transporting water via tankers in desperate attempts to preserve their growing yields.

Comparison With Prior Administration

During his address, Rao contrasted current conditions with the policies of the preceding ten-year BRS administration led by former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekar Rao. He highlighted past provisions including continuous electricity supply for farming operations, expanded irrigation infrastructure, and the timely disbursement of agricultural support funds through the Rythu Bandhu initiative.

Additional welfare programs from the prior administration, such as financial assistance schemes and paddy procurement operations during the COVID-19 pandemic, were also cited as benchmarks of previous governance.

Political Context and Upcoming Events

Beyond agricultural grievances, Rao criticized the current administration for unfulfilled electoral commitments, questioning the timeline of implementation for policies promised during campaign periods.

Looking ahead, the BRS leadership announced plans to host a major public gathering in Nirmal scheduled for November 11, where additional local politicians are anticipated to formally align with the party.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers seeking to understand the ongoing political discourse regarding Telangana's agricultural sector can review the official context through primary reporting.

What is Confirmed:

  • KT Rama Rao made these statements at Telangana Bhavan during a party induction event.
  • Specific criticisms included allegations regarding the Kaleshwaram project pumps, Godavari and Krishna river water usage, and shortages of urea, power, and irrigation water.
  • The BRS has scheduled a public meeting in Nirmal for November 11.

What Remains Unverified:

  • Independent verification of the administrative decisions regarding project operations or resource distribution has not been provided in the source text.
  • Claims regarding the precise extent of crop losses and utility shortages represent partisan political assertions rather than independent agronomic audits.

How to Check: Readers can examine the original reporting and ongoing coverage through the official Times of India portal at [The Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/hyderabad/ktr-alleges-government-failure-behind-drought-conditions-in-telangana/articleshow/135234516.cms).
